# Helm values reference

Chart `deploy/helm/roracle` (generated from values.yaml). One row per key: block maps are expanded, inline maps and lists are shown whole. Descriptions are the comments in values.yaml; see the [deployment guide](../enterprise/deployment-guide.md) for how the values fit together.

## general

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `imagePullSecrets` | `[]` | [{name: regcred}] |
| `nameOverride` | `""` |  |
| `fullnameOverride` | `""` |  |
| `metrics` | `{"enabled": true}` | Prometheus /metrics on api (8000) and worker (healthPort): adds prometheus.io/* pod annotations. Never routed via ingress. |

## global

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `global.imageRegistry` | `""` | prefix for every image, e.g. registry.internal.example |

## rerank

Reranker (cross-encoder; deploy/game-01). Empty url = off. Allow its CIDR/port in networkPolicy.egressCIDRs.llm. Recommended on (own-corpus-v1 PASS, docs/eval/2026-11-16-rerank.md): set url to your site's TEI endpoint.

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `rerank.url` | `""` | site-specific; TEI binds 127.0.0.1 on game-01: use a TLS proxy/mesh URL, e.g. https://rerank.internal/rerank |
| `rerank.api` | `tei` | cohere \| tei (deploy/game-01 serves TEI) |
| `rerank.model` | `bge-reranker-v2-m3` | sent to cohere-style servers; TEI ignores it |

## migrate

Pre-upgrade hook Job (pre-install too for external Postgres; post-install for bundled CNPG, which waits <= 10 min for the DB so api/worker may restart until it finishes): `python -m roracle migrate`. Failure blocks the release. Use `helm --timeout 30m`. Env is inlined (the ConfigMap does not exist yet on pre-install). Runs as the namespace default ServiceAccount (no token mounted) because the chart ServiceAccount is not yet created either.

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `migrate.activeDeadlineSeconds` | `1500` |  |
| `migrate.resources.requests` | `{"cpu": "500m", "memory": "512Mi"}` |  |
| `migrate.resources.limits` | `{"memory": "512Mi"}` |  |
| `migrate.runAsUser` | `10001` |  |

## postgres

Data services: operator CRs (CNPG, ECK must be installed by the platform) Each can be switched to "external": nothing is rendered; point the app at your own service via config / secrets.existingSecret. Credentials are always secret names + keys, never values. Backups go to the external S3 (buckets below); for real DR keep them on a different cluster/site.

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `postgres.mode` | `cnpg` | cnpg \| external (external: ROR_DATABASE_URL in existingSecret, nothing rendered) |
| `postgres.instances` | `3` |  |
| `postgres.image` | `{"repository": "ghcr.io/cloudnative-pg/postgresql", "tag": "16.6", "digest": "", "pullPolicy": "IfNotPresent"}` |  |
| `postgres.storage` | `{"size": "100Gi", "storageClass": ""}` |  |
| `postgres.resources.requests` | `{"cpu": "2", "memory": "8Gi"}` |  |
| `postgres.resources.limits` | `{"memory": "8Gi"}` |  |
| `postgres.parameters` | `{"max_connections": "200", "shared_buffers": "2GB", "work_mem": "16MB", "jit": "off"}` | postgresql.parameters; archive_timeout is forced to 5min; it bounds the RPO (about 5 min) only while WAL is being produced. max_connections is checked against the replica budget at render time; shared_buffers ~ 25% of resources.limits.memory. NB: a `parameters` override without max_connections leaves PostgreSQL's own default (100), which the guard then uses. jit off: see docs/perf/report-2026-11-17.md (F1) |
| `postgres.reservedConnections` | `15` | superuser_reserved (3) + CNPG/monitoring/replication + migrate Job + operator headroom |
| `postgres.pooler` | `{"enabled": false, "instances": 2, "poolMode": "transaction", "maxClientConn": 1000, "defaultPoolSize": 40}` | PgBouncer (CNPG Pooler, transaction mode). When enabled, point ROR_DATABASE_URL at <release>-pg-pooler-rw and keep the migrate Job on the direct <release>-pg-rw service. Server connections = instances x defaultPoolSize. |
| `postgres.appCredentialsSecret` | `""` | REQUIRED (cnpg): kubernetes.io/basic-auth Secret (username roracle, password) for the app owner. ROR_DATABASE_URL (postgresql+psycopg://...) stays in secrets.existingSecret: CNPG's generated uri lacks +psycopg. |
| `postgres.monitoring` | `{"enabled": true}` | PodMonitor + CNPG custom queries (roracle_archiver; roracle_jobs is no longer used by the dashboard). Needs prometheus-operator CRDs. spec.monitoring.enablePodMonitor is deprecated upstream (still works); if it is removed, create the PodMonitor from the observability values instead. |
| `postgres.backup.enabled` | `true` |  |
| `postgres.backup.method` | `plugin` | plugin: barman-cloud plugin (ObjectStore CR, CNPG >= 1.26; plugin + cert-manager must be installed). barmanObjectStore: legacy in-tree config (deprecated upstream, still works). |
| `postgres.backup.destinationPath` | `s3://roracle-pg-backup/` |  |
| `postgres.backup.endpointURL` | `""` | REQUIRED when backup.enabled: S3 endpoint URL (https://...) |
| `postgres.backup.credentialsSecret` | `{"name": "", "accessKeyKey": "ACCESS_KEY_ID", "secretAccessKeyKey": "ACCESS_SECRET_KEY"}` | REQUIRED when enabled |
| `postgres.backup.endpointCA` | `{"name": "", "key": "ca.crt"}` | optional Secret holding the CA of a TLS object store |
| `postgres.backup.retentionPolicy` | `30d` |  |
| `postgres.backup.schedule` | `0 0 2 * * *` | 6-field cron (seconds first): daily base backup 02:00 |
| `postgres.backup.serverName` | `""` | archive path name; "" = cluster name. MUST be new (differs from the source) after a recovery |
| `postgres.recovery` | `{"enabled": false, "targetTime": "", "sourceServerName": ""}` | PITR: bootstrap the Helm-managed cluster from backups instead of initdb (docs/enterprise/backup-dr.md). Needs backup.enabled + a new backup.serverName. targetTime "" = latest; sourceServerName "" = cluster name |

## parsers

Parser services: optional in-chart Deployments. Only the worker calls them (ingest pipeline + evidence scan). Backend URL settings are auto-filled (roracle.endpoints) when enabled and config.ROR_* is empty; to use an external parser set enabled=false and fill config.ROR_*. NetworkPolicy gives parsers NO egress (see networkPolicy). Per parser: writableDirs = emptyDirs (readOnlyRootFilesystem stays true unless overridden); runAsUser = image uid; probe = {path} (HTTP) or {tcp: true}; args/env passed through; image tag is mandatory (no appVersion default).

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `parsers.gotenberg.enabled` | `true` |  |

Fail closed: AlertExceedsMax yes and limits >= the upload/evidence caps (template fails if lower: config.ROR_MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES, ROR_EVIDENCE_MAX_BYTES). ClamAV maximum is < 4G. Suffix K/M/G. |

## connectors

Connector egress (worker only; backend also enforces connector_http_allow_cidrs). Default none.

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `connectors.egressCIDRs` | `[]` |  |
| `connectors.ports` | `[443]` |  |

## caBundle

Merged CA bundle for api/worker/migrate: an init container writes certifi's bundle + the CAs below into an emptyDir that is mounted over certifi's cacert.pem (elastic_transport ignores SSL_CERT_FILE when certifi is installed); SSL_CERT_FILE/REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE/AWS_CA_BUNDLE and ROR_ELASTIC_CA_CERTS/ROR_S3_CA_BUNDLE point at it. Active only when ES TLS (eck) or extraSecrets (e.g. the S3 CA) are in play.

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `caBundle.certifiPath` | `/app/backend/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/certifi/cacert.pem` | coupled to the backend image layout |
| `caBundle.extraSecrets` | `[]` | [{name: my-ca, key: ca.crt}] operator CAs for external ES/S3/etc. |

## networkPolicy

Data-tier policies (data-postgres/es) are always rendered for bundled modes. Namespace values are matched by label kubernetes.io/metadata.name.

| Key | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `networkPolicy.operatorNamespaces` | `{"eck": "elastic-system", "cnpg": "cnpg-system"}` |  |
| `networkPolicy.monitoringNamespace` | `monitoring` |  |
| `networkPolicy.kubeAPI` | `{"cidrs": [], "ports": [443, 6443]}` | Instance managers / operators need the kube-apiserver. Empty cidrs = allow these ports to any destination; tighten. |
| `networkPolicy.s3` | `{"cidrs": [], "ports": [443, 9000], "namespaceSelector": {}, "podSelector": {}}` | Object storage egress for api/worker/migrate and the data tier (CNPG barman, ES snapshots): CIDRs and/or an in-cluster peer (e.g. Rook-Ceph RGW: namespaceSelector + podSelector, ports = post-DNAT container ports). |
| `networkPolicy.dns.namespace` | `kube-system` |  |
| `networkPolicy.dns.podLabels` | `{"k8s-app": "kube-dns"}` |  |
| `networkPolicy.enabled` | `true` | Application tier (enabled: default-deny ingress+egress for every pod in the release namespace + allow rules). |
| `networkPolicy.ingressNamespaceSelector` | `{"kubernetes.io/metadata.name": "ingress-nginx"}` | namespace labels of the ingress controller |
| `networkPolicy.externalCIDRs.postgres` | `{"cidrs": [], "ports": [5432]}` |  |
| `networkPolicy.externalCIDRs.elasticsearch` | `{"cidrs": [], "ports": [9200]}` |  |
| `networkPolicy.egressCIDRs.llm` | `{"cidrs": [], "ports": [443], "namespaceSelector": {}, "podSelector": {}}` |  |
| `networkPolicy.egressCIDRs.oidc` | `{"cidrs": [], "ports": [443], "namespaceSelector": {}, "podSelector": {}}` |  |
| `networkPolicy.egressCIDRs.otel` | `{"cidrs": [], "ports": [4318], "namespaceSelector": {}, "podSelector": {}}` |  |
| `networkPolicy.egressCIDRs.parsers` | `{"cidrs": [], "ports": [3000, 5001, 8070, 3310], "namespaceSelector": {}, "podSelector": {}}` |  |
| `networkPolicy.scrape` | `{"enabled": true, "ports": [8000, 8001]}` | allow monitoringNamespace -> api/worker /metrics (match worker.healthPort) |
